t: Personal AI OS: what actually makes AI smarter
s: Not more skills: good memory (organized Markdown), a few sharp skills, real tools (search, code, files) and verification. Skills teach how; MCP connects tools; memory gives context.
x: Order: memory → 3 skills → shared workspace → tools → automation + review.
Skills load only when relevant, so a few precise ones beat many overlapping ones.

s: A skill is a folder with SKILL.md: a name, a description that says when to use it, and instructions. Claude loads it only when the task matches the description.
x: Write the description as triggers: 'Use when I…'.
Keep one skill per recurring workflow.

s: Model Context Protocol: an open standard that lets AI apps use external tools and data (Drive, GitHub, browsers) through 'servers'. Add one only for a real workflow and check its permissions.
CLAUDE.md files load automatically at session start: project rules, preferences, key facts. Keep them short and point to other files for detail.

t: Second brain method: CODE + PARA (Tiago Forte)
s: CODE = Capture (save what resonates, don't over-filter), Organize, Distill (pull out the key points over time), Express (turn notes into output). PARA files by actionability: Projects, Areas, Resources, Archives.
x: The goal is output (projects, content), not a pretty archive.
Organize by project, not by topic: 'where will I use this?'

s: One idea per note, titled as a claim, densely linked to other notes, rewritten over time. Links beat folders: an atomic note can be reused by every topic it touches.
x: Built on Niklas Luhmann's Zettelkasten.
Write notes for yourself; refine them each time you revisit.

s: Workflows: AI + tools follow fixed code paths. Agents: the model decides its own steps and tool use. Start with the simplest solution; agents trade cost and speed for flexibility.
x: Successful teams use simple, composable patterns, not heavy frameworks.
Predictable steps → workflow (like my systems/). Open-ended tasks → agent.

s: What the AI sees matters more than clever prompts. Context is a limited attention budget: more text can lower accuracy ('context rot'). Keep instructions small, tools few and clear, and load details just in time.
x: Claude Code pattern: CLAUDE.md up front, files searched on demand (grep/glob).
Long tasks: compaction, structured notes, sub-agents.

s: 'LLM as an operating system': core memory always in context, recall memory (past conversations, searchable), archival memory (long-term, searchable). The agent edits its own memory and consolidates it while idle.
x: Paper: 'MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems' (UC Berkeley, 2023); now Letta, open source.
Memory degrades without pruning and consolidation.

t: How my AI OS maps to the research
s: Core memory = CLAUDE.md + memory/CONTEXT.md. Recall = brain/log.md. Archival = Second Brain stars + Drive vault. Workflows = systems/. Consolidation = Daily optimizer. Gap: app notes don't reach Claude's memory yet.
x: Next upgrades: weekly consolidation (merge, prune, link), app → Drive bridge, distill notes into atomic stars.

t: Finfluencer rules (EU + Belgium): educate, don't advise
s: Explaining how investing works is allowed. Telling followers what to buy/sell, especially tailored to them, can be investment advice, which in Belgium needs FSMA authorization. EU market-abuse rules: say who you are, be objective, disclose conflicts (holdings, partners). Paid posts must be labeled.
x: Investedia guardrails: education + examples, no 'buy X' calls, disclose own positions and sponsors, add 'not financial advice / for education'.
Never promote unauthorized platforms or products: can make you complicit in fraud.
Not legal advice: check FSMA's own guidance before monetizing.

t: ESMA: investment recommendations on social media
s: ESMA and national supervisors state that anyone recommending investments on social media falls under the Market Abuse Regulation: identify yourself, present recommendations objectively, disclose interests. Breaches can mean fines or referral to prosecutors.
x: Reported (unverified): ESMA finfluencer factsheet, Jan 2026: responsibility for content, label paid promotions, no misleading claims.

t: Instagram Reels: watch time, likes and sends per reach
s: Instagram's head Adam Mosseri reportedly named three key Reels signals: watch time (most important), likes per reach (reach among followers) and sends per reach (reach to new people). Insights now split follower vs non-follower reach.
x: For Investedia: strong first 2 seconds (watch time), content people DM to a friend ('send this to someone who…') for new reach.
Specific multipliers (e.g. sends worth 3-5x likes) have no primary source.

s: Market-data/education sites: TradingView (~209M visits/mo), Finviz (~17.8M), Stock Analysis (~8.4M, built by one founder since 2019). Winners own one clear promise or tool, rank a page per ticker/term in Google, and grow a free newsletter.
x: Estimates from Semrush; check the same month in one tool before comparing.
Details and actions: memory/projects/investedia-competitors.md

s: The big sites cover everything; winners own one clear promise. Candidate: markets explained for young Europeans, one chart and one sentence.
A page per stock or term that answers one question in plain language. Stock Analysis gets most traffic from ticker searches.
'3 market moves explained in 60 seconds'. An email list is an audience you own; Market Bullets reportedly reached ~168k readers.
One concept per video, strong first 2 seconds, a reason to send it to a friend. Top of funnel to the site.
Finviz is known for its heat map. Idea: a 'what moved today and why' page.
Explain how investing works with examples; no 'buy X' calls, disclose own positions and sponsors, label ads, add 'for education, not financial advice'.

t: The first 2 seconds decide a Reel
s: Watch time is the strongest Reels signal, so the opening must earn the next second: a surprising number, a question, or a visible result.

t: Sends bring new people, likes keep followers
s: Likes per reach mostly helps reach among followers; DM sends help reach non-followers. Write content people want to forward.
Sending only the most relevant notes saves tokens and can improve accuracy ('context rot'). Small instructions, few clear tools.
Notes and AI memory degrade without merging duplicates, pruning stale items and adding links. The weekly review does this.
Atomic, linked notes can be reused by every topic they touch, which makes the galaxy smarter than long mixed notes.
tests/smoke.js opens the app at phone and desktop size with a fake AI and checks errors, panels, Ask, data integrity and edits. Runs on GitHub every push and nightly; costs no AI tokens.
Edit only app/index.html; tools/build-claude-page.py builds the Claude page from it, so changes aren't made twice.
Research saved in app/knowledge.json appears as stars on every device; Ask and Talk use it.
Repeatable check of competitors: same-source traffic estimates, features, formats, 1-3 ranked actions. Say 'check competitors'.
